frequency_question: How often do announced major tariffs take effect on schedule without being delayed, rescinded, or replaced by a negotiated agreement?
membership_rule: Members are explicit tariff threats made by the executive branch carrying a defined implementation date. Excluded are routine antidumping/countervailing duty administrative tariff adjustments and vague explorations of trade policy.

cases.name: Reagan Japanese auto import quotas/tariffs threat
Bush Sr. threatened tariffs on EU oilseeds
Clinton threatened sanctions on Japan auto parts
Trump Section 232 steel and aluminum tariffs
Trump threatened tariffs on Mexico over immigration
Trump threatened 100% tariffs on French wine

coverage_note: 8 named prominent tariff threats; approximately 15 to 20 total major executive tariff threats since 1980 meeting the criteria, with similar low-realization rates due to use of threats as negotiating leverage.
known_gaps: Excludes minor sectoral disputes handled solely through low-level WTO or administrative channels.
validity_reason: Executive branch tariff threat dynamics and the tendency to use them as leverage remain structurally consistent across administrations.
